source.title: From Trait Vectors to Circuits: Tracing Refusal and Sycophancy Through Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly replicates the refusal-direction projection result on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, using a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation direction and testing refusal after projection.
record.gate_note: The refusal projection, refusal-direction steering, and refusal-circuit interventions are included. The sycophancy experiments concern a different behavior and are excluded. Circuit faithfulness and coordinate-reconstruction scores without a refusal-behavior outcome are not rows; the study also cites other work on multiple refusal directions and harmfulness encoding, but those are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The study extracts the Arditi et al. harmful-minus-harmless direction at layer 15 in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It projects it out and steers against it, measures refusal log-odds and WildGuard refusal rates, and calls the result a replication of [1]. The circuit analyses are its own extension and test reconstruction and transmission circuits, not the direction claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say the refusal direction causally changes refusal, replicating Arditi et al. in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Refusal admits a compact reconstruction and transmission decomposition under the tested counterfactuals, and coordinate restoration is near-sufficient for the ablated prompt-end signal. They stress that steering-transmission circuits are not necessarily the natural computation, and they explicitly do not claim all natural refusal is one-dimensional.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction and projection intervention in a new instruct model, and explicitly calls the result a replication. It also studies selected-layer projection, circuit ablation/restoration, and recurrent steering; it does not test adding the direction to induce harmless-request refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: The study distinguishes layer-15 projection from global projection over all layers, prompt-end refusal log-odds from free-generation refusal labels, and multiple circuit interventions. The authors note that vector extraction and intervention depend on data, formatting, pooling, layer, sign, and token positions; EAP-IG depends on its path and baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: A 699-edge connected graph reconstructs the layer-15 refusal coordinate after global projection (F 98.84%, N 93.90%). An 8,000-edge graph transmits recurrent anti-refusal steering (93.4% of the effect; ablating it blocks steering). A two-stage circuit is more edge-efficient than direct circuit discovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The computation around the refusal direction decomposes into compact upstream reconstruction and downstream transmission circuits.

record.problems: Only one model is studied. The authors state that refusal reconstruction tests recovery after a defined projection rather than natural harmful-input-to-coordinate formation, and that scalar restoration measures one prompt-end logit metric. The two-stage comparison transfers a complete circuit-restricted layer-15 state rather than only the scalar. Several intervention results are reported without uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted circuit faithfulness/necessity and coordinate-reconstruction scores that do not report refusal behavior, and sycophancy results because they measure a different behavior. The paper’s static faithfulness comparisons and associated edge-count results are in Section 5.3; they are not refusal-rate outcomes.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of general capabilities; models other than Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
All: no jailbreaks or adversarial training.
All: multi-direction structure is cited, not tested for refusal.
All: PolyRefuse prompts are used, but no cross-language transfer is tested.

missing.what: Global projection free-generation refusal on the Section 5.3 64-prompt set: 98.44% to 31.25% (CI 20.31-42.19%). This is a direct V1 removal result, currently embedded only as R15's baseline.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label over all circuit rows is dropped: those rows test circuits, not the direction claim, and are moved to fits_no_version. The sycophancy results concern a different behaviour and are correctly excluded. Only one model is studied, and no capability check is reported. Text and figure caption disagree on which graph was ablated before restoration (R6/R8).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test adding the direction to induce refusals to harmless requests or whether general capabilities remain largely intact. It tests one instruct model and selected refusal settings.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is tested.
No jailbreak attack is tested, and no training against ablation is performed.

The study does not test whether refusal is better represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions. Its discussion of sycophancy dimensionality and citations to prior refusal work do not test this version.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No refusal-training method or training stage is varied.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: layer-15 or global projection, negative steering, and coordinate restoration on held-out harmful prompts
relationships.reason: Projection drops log-odds from 4.943 to -4.064 or -12.642 and refusal from 93.8% to 6.3%, or from 100% to 0% (R1-R3, R19). Steering at -2 cuts refusal from 98.44% to 3.13% (R10). Restoring the coordinate alone recovers 94.2% (R8).
relationships.display_finding: Projection reduced refusal log-odds from 4.943 to −4.064 or −12.642 and refusal from 93.8% to 6.3% or 100% to 0%; steering at −2 reduced refusal from 98.44% to 3.13%, and restoring the coordinate recovered 94.2% refusal.

relation.reason: Q1 tests directly whether changing the refusal coordinate changes refusal, and reports its own ablation, steering and restoration results.

tranche.reason: The study uses Arditi's harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, chooses the layer by Arditi's causal criteria, and projects the direction out. It measures Arditi's refusal log-odds, adds a WildGuard free-generation rate, and calls the result a replication of [1] in Section 7.

source_check.notes: A row is missing: Sec 5.3 free generation, normal 98.44% (CI 95.31–100%) → global projection 31.25% (CI 20.31–42.19%), WildGuard, 64 prompts. It should be linked to V1 with state partial. The difference from Sec 5.1's 93.8%→6.3% is unexplained in the text, and synthesis statements should not attribute it to prompt set. The study covers one model only, with no capability or harmless-prompt induction test. Appendix D evaluator prompts are quoted judge prompts, not instructions to the reader.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, global projection, WildGuard-judged free generation: 98.44%→31.25% (95% CI 20.31–42.19%) in Sec 5.3 and 93.8%→6.3% in Sec 5.1, each on 64 prompts. The text does not say whether the prompts differ. Normal refusal also differs between the runs (93.8% vs 98.44%) for unstated reasons. The same paper reports 100%→0% on a separate 16-prompt test.
statements.problem: Both pairs of numbers are correct. But the text never says that the 98.44%→31.25% and 93.8%→6.3% runs use different prompt sets. Both are described only as 'free generation on 64 prompts', and Appendix A describes one fixed 64-question circuit-evaluation subset.

statements.correction: 2609.22224 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, global projection): 98.44%→31.25% (Sec 5.3, 64 prompts); 93.8%→6.3% (Sec 5.1, 64 prompts); 100%→0% (Sec 5.3, 16 prompts); log-odds 4.943→−12.642. Steering at −2 at layer 15: 98.44%→3.13%. Whether the two 64-prompt runs share prompts is not stated (App. A: one fixed 64-question circuit-evaluation subset). The study's results span both sides of the conflict, so it is internally mixed, not weak.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but listing the study only on the 'Weak' side misreads it. Under the same global projection it also reports near-complete removal, and 'another 64-prompt set' is not stated in the text.

statements.correction: Global projection, free generation, WildGuard: 93.8%→6.3% (Sec 5.1, R3) and 98.44%→31.25% (Sec 5.3, R15 baseline/text), each on '64 prompts'. The cause of the difference is unstated; normal refusal also differs (93.8% vs 98.44%). R19 is 100%→0% on a separate 16-prompt test.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. The factor 'prompt set' is not supported: the text does not say the two 64-prompt runs differ in prompts. The cited row R19 (100%→0%, 16 prompts) is not the 98.44%→31.25% pair, which comes from the Sec 5.3 text (R15 baseline).
